checks.requirement: All 195 catalog flag assets decode in Chromium with HTTP 200, image/png, expected SHA-256, and positive dimensions.
checks.evidence: browser-result.json records total 195, 195 unique URLs/digests, and positive dimensions; browser-raw.json has actual_exit 0 and success true.

checks.requirement: Negative controls reject HTML and a missing flag.
The media set used by the run matches a fresh public catalog snapshot.
checks.evidence: catalog-identity.json records HTTP 200, 195 public questions, exact set match, and equal fresh/used raw SHA-256 values.

checks.requirement: Saved receipts and screenshots are internally consistent.
checks.evidence: All review-input hashes matched; the parsed raw return's result equals browser-result.json; decoded-samples.png and reported-flag.png were viewed.

checks.requirement: Root-owned local resources were cleaned up.
checks.evidence: run-notes.json records server exit 0, no listener on the loopback port, and successful named-browser close.

strengths: The browser script validates transport status, MIME, content digest, and actual bitmap decoding rather than relying on DOM image load alone.
The content-addressed filename and browser-computed SHA-256 bind each fetched response to the catalog media identity.
The negative controls cover a wrong MIME type and a missing resource; concurrency is bounded at eight.
limits: The test uses an isolated loopback static server and does not exercise the Flutter client or production delivery stack.
The saved visual samples are corroborating evidence only; the complete 195-item proof is the structured Chromium result.

reviewer_execution: No browser, server, test, build, child process, or vendor CLI was executed by this reviewer. Review used saved files, hash comparison, parsed-receipt consistency checks, and image viewing only.
release_boundary: This is not Flutter, nginx/container, deployment, feedback-resolution, release, external-acceptance, or publication approval.
